entries.question: Which Python libraries do you use daily, and how do they fit together?
aliases: which python libraries do you use daily
what python libraries do you use
how do pandas numpy and scikit learn fit together
what is your python data science stack
which libraries do you use for machine learning
what is your python stack for ai
how do you use fastapi and pydantic
walk me through your daily python tools
entries.answer_en: I use Pandas to clean tables, NumPy for fast number work, and Scikit-learn to train small models. Hugging Face handles text and embeddings. FastAPI serves the API. Pydantic checks every model output before my code trusts it.
entries.followup_en: In the early-warning work I loaded sheets with Pandas, built the features, then trained a classifier with Scikit-learn. For BTEC question generation I call the model through FastAPI, and I force JSON with Pydantic. So a bad shape never reaches a teacher. I keep the stack small on purpose. Extra libraries make an audit harder.
entries.answer_ar: أستخدم بايثون يومياً: بانداس ونمباي وسايكت ليرن للجداول والنماذج الصغيرة، وفاست إيه بي آي وبيدانتك للواجهة والتحقق من المخرجات.

entries.question: What is data leakage?
aliases: what is leakage in machine learning
why did my model score look too good
can the test set leak into training
entries.answer_en: Data leakage is when information from outside the training set is used to train the model, causing overly optimistic performance. Example: using future data to predict the past. I prevent it by careful train-test splitting and feature selection.
entries.followup_en: Time leakage is another form: you use later months to predict earlier ones. A feature can also leak if it is only filled after the outcome is known. I treat a surprisingly high score as a warning, not a win. Split first, then fit every transform on train only.
entries.answer_ar: تسرب البيانات هو عندما تُستخدم معلومات من خارج مجموعة التدريب لتدريب النموذج، مما يسبب أداءً متفائلاً بشكل مفرط. مثال: استخدام بيانات المستقبل للتنبؤ بالماضي. أمنعه بالتقسيم الدقيق للتدريب والاختبار واختيار الميزات.

entries.question: How do you prevent data leakage?
aliases: how do you prevent data leakage
how do you avoid data leakage
how do you protect against leakage
how do you split time series data
should I put scaling in a pipeline
how do you keep the test set clean
entries.answer_en: I split first, then transform. Scaling and encoding live inside a Scikit-learn Pipeline so they fit on train only. If the data has time order, I split by time, not at random. I also drop any column that is really a copy of the label.
entries.followup_en: In the school early-warning project the rows followed terms, so a random split would have mixed the future into the past. A pipeline makes that mistake harder because the test fold never fits the scaler. After training I still ask: would this field exist at decision time? If not, it does not belong in the model.
entries.answer_ar: أمنع التسريب بفصل البيانات أولاً ثم التحويل داخل بايبلاين، وأقسم حسب الزمن إن كان للبيانات ترتيب زمني.

entries.question: Why Scikit-learn and not a neural network?
aliases: why scikit learn and not a neural network
when do you use deep learning versus classical ml
why not use deep learning for tabular data
do we need a neural net for this table
when is a simple model enough
entries.answer_en: For medium tabular data, Scikit-learn or tree models usually win and are easier to explain. I use a neural net for text, audio, images, or very large custom work. I start with the simplest model that works, then go deeper only if the numbers say so.
entries.followup_en: Early-warning and helpdesk were tables with a few thousand rows. A neural net would have been slower to train and harder to explain to a teacher or a supervisor. Deep learning earned its place later, for Whisper and for LLMs, not for those school spreadsheets.
entries.answer_ar: للبيانات الجدولية متوسطة الحجم أبدأ بسايكت ليرن لأنه أوضح وأسهل تفسيراً، والشبكات العميقة للنص أو الصوت أو الصور.

entries.question: Explain precision, recall, and F1
aliases: what is the difference between precision and recall
when do you use recall instead of accuracy
why is accuracy a bad metric
which metric for a rare class
entries.answer_en: Precision is: of the cases the model flagged, how many were really right. Recall is: of the real cases, how many did it catch. F1 balances the two. Accuracy lies when one class is rare, so I pick the metric by the cost of the mistake.
entries.followup_en: In the early-warning work, missing a student who needed help was worse than a false alarm. So I pushed recall, and I watched precision, so teachers were not flooded. A model that flags nobody can still look 80 percent accurate. And it is useless. That is why I always show the confusion matrix next to the headline score.
entries.answer_ar: الدقة تعني كم من التنبيهات صحيحة، والاستدعاء يعني كم من الحالات الحقيقية التقطناها، وأختار المقياس حسب ثمن الخطأ لا حسب العادة.

entries.question: How do you evaluate a classification model?
aliases: how do you evaluate a classification model
what metrics do you use for classification
how do you measure a classifier
how do you validate a classification model
do you use a holdout set
how do you compare against a baseline
how do you know the classifier is good
entries.answer_en: I use accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. For imbalanced data, I focus on precision, recall, and F1. In the helpdesk classification project, I used F1-score because some departments had fewer tickets.
entries.followup_en: For helpdesk tickets I cared that rare departments were not dumped into Other. For students I looked at recall on the at-risk class. If one school or one department is much worse, the average is lying. A model that only beats the majority-class baseline by a little is not ready.
entries.answer_ar: أستخدم الدقة، والضبط، والاستدعاء، ودرجة F1، و ROC-AUC. بالنسبة للبيانات غير المتوازنة، أركز على الضبط والاستدعاء و F1. في مشروع تصنيف مكتب المساعدة، استخدمت درجة F1 لأن بعض الأقسام لديها تذاكر أقل.

entries.question: What is overfitting?
aliases: why is training accuracy high and test low
entries.answer_en: Overfitting means the model learned noise in the training data, so it looks great there and worse on new data. Underfitting is the opposite: the model is too simple and weak on both. A big gap between train and validation is the signal.
entries.followup_en: On small school tables it is easy to overfit if you add too many features or a deep tree. I watch the gap, not only the training score. If both scores are low, I need a better signal or a richer model, not more regularization.
entries.answer_ar: الإفراط في التعلّم يعني أن النموذج حفظ ضجيج التدريب فيبدو قوياً ثم يضعف على بيانات جديدة، والعكس هو التبسيط الزائد.

entries.question: How do you prevent overfitting?
aliases: how do you know your model generalizes
how do you keep a honest test set
entries.answer_en: I keep a hold-out set I never tune on. I start with a simple model, add regularization, and use cleaner data before a fancier algorithm. For iterative training I stop early. Cross-validation must respect time or groups if those matter.
entries.followup_en: In the student project I did not shuffle across terms. That is a generalization choice, not a detail. More features can make overfitting worse if they are noisy. I would rather a slightly weaker model that holds on new terms than a perfect training score.
entries.answer_ar: أمنع الإفراط بمجموعة اختبار ثابتة ونموذج أبسط وتنظيم أوضح، والتحقق المتقاطع يجب أن يحترم الزمن أو المجموعات.

entries.question: How do you handle imbalanced data?
aliases: how do you handle imbalanced data
what do you do when one class is rare
how do you deal with class imbalance
most of my labels are zero
should I oversample the rare class
do you change the decision threshold
entries.answer_en: I stop using accuracy. I pick precision, recall, or F1 from the cost of the error. Then I try class weights, a better threshold, and only then resampling. I always report the rare class, not only the average.
entries.followup_en: The default 50 percent cutoff is usually wrong when the rare class is 5 percent of rows. In early-warning most students were fine, so I optimized recall on the at-risk group and watched false alarms. Weights inside the model are simpler to ship than a heavy resampling pipeline.
entries.answer_ar: مع اختلال الفئات أترك مقياس الصحة وأضبط العتبة أو أوزان الفئات حسب ثمن الخطأ، وأراقب أداء الفئة النادرة.

entries.question: What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
aliases: what is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning
when do you cluster instead of classify
do you need labels for this
entries.answer_en: Supervised learning needs labels: past cases with the right answer. Classification predicts a category. Regression predicts a number. Unsupervised learning has no labels. Clustering just groups similar rows. Most of my project work was supervised classification.
entries.followup_en: Helpdesk tickets had department labels, so that was classification. Early-warning was also supervised: at-risk or not. I would cluster only to explore, for example to see if tickets form new groups the labels missed. I would not ship a cluster as a decision without a human mapping those groups.
entries.answer_ar: التعلّم الخاضع للإشراف يحتاج أمثلة معلّمة للتنبؤ بفئة أو رقم، وبدونه نكتفي بتجميع المتشابه دون تسميات جاهزة.

entries.question: What is machine learning?
aliases: explain machine learning in simple terms
how is machine learning different from rules
entries.answer_en: Machine learning means the system learns patterns from examples instead of us writing every rule. I give it past cases, it finds the relationship, then it scores new cases it has never seen.
entries.followup_en: A rule says: if attendance is below a limit, flag the student. A model can mix attendance, grades, and history, without me listing every case by hand. That is useful. But it can also learn the wrong shortcut. So I still check leakage and metrics, and whether a teacher can act on the score.
entries.answer_ar: تعلّم الآلة يعني أن النظام يستخرج أنماطاً من أمثلة سابقة بدل كتابة كل قاعدة يدوياً، ثم يطبّقها على حالات جديدة.

entries.question: What is deep learning?
aliases: why do neural nets need so much data
when do you use deep learning
entries.answer_en: Deep learning is machine learning with many-layer neural nets. The extra layers learn features by themselves. That is why it powers speech, vision, and LLMs. It needs more data and more compute, and it is harder to explain.
entries.followup_en: I used it where the input is language or sound: Whisper for the kiosk, and LLMs for BTEC text. For school tables I still start with Scikit-learn, because a teacher needs a reason, not only a score. Deep is not automatically better.
entries.answer_ar: التعلّم العميق شبكات عصبية متعددة الطبقات تتعلّم الميزات وحدها، وهو مناسب للنص والصوت والصورة أكثر من الجداول الصغيرة.

entries.question: What is the difference between AI, machine learning, and deep learning?
aliases: what is the difference between ai machine learning and deep learning
ai versus machine learning versus deep learning
is deep learning the same as machine learning
is chatgpt machine learning or ai
are ai machine learning and deep learning competing products
entries.answer_en: AI is the wide field: machines doing tasks that look intelligent. Machine learning is the part that learns from data. Deep learning is machine learning with neural nets. Generative AI creates text or images, usually with deep models. One sits inside the other. They are not rival products.
entries.followup_en: A rules engine can be called AI and use no learning at all. My helpdesk classifier is ML without deep learning. Whisper and LLMs are deep learning. When someone says we need AI, I ask which of those they actually mean, because the build and the risk are different.
entries.answer_ar: الذكاء الاصطناعي حقل واسع، وتعلّم الآلة جزء منه يتعلّم من البيانات، والتعلّم العميق شبكات عصبية داخله، والتوليدي يُنشئ محتوى.

entries.question: What is the difference between TF-IDF and embeddings?
aliases: what is the difference between tf idf and embeddings
when do you use tf idf versus embeddings
entries.answer_en: TF-IDF scores words by how often they appear, balanced by how common they are. Embeddings capture meaning, so two sentences with different words can sit close. I used TF-IDF for helpdesk tickets and embeddings for assignment similarity, because students change the words on purpose.
entries.followup_en: If the error is missing a synonym, embeddings help. If the error is ignoring a required keyword, TF-IDF or hybrid search is better. I do not jump to embeddings for every text task. The helpdesk needed stable categories and speed, not a vector database.
entries.answer_ar: تي إف آي دي إف يعتمد تكرار الكلمات، أما التضمين فيقارب المعنى حتى لو اختلفت الألفاظ، ولذلك استخدمتهما لمهمتين مختلفتين.

entries.question: What is TF-IDF?
aliases: how do you turn tickets into numbers
why do stop words get low weight
entries.answer_en: TF-IDF means term frequency times inverse document frequency. A word that is common in one ticket and rare overall gets a high weight. Words like the almost disappear. It is bag-of-words: fast and clear when the exact words matter.
entries.followup_en: I used it at Al Najat to classify helpdesk tickets into departments. No LLM, no RAG. The model is a classic classifier on those weights. It fails when people paraphrase, which is why I did not use it for the assignment similarity checker.
entries.answer_ar: تي إف آي دي إف يزن الكلمة حسب تكرارها في النص وندرتها في بقية الوثائق، وهو مناسب عندما تهمّ الألفاظ حرفياً كما في تصنيف التذاكر.

entries.question: What is model drift?
aliases: why did the model get worse this year
the data changed after we trained
entries.answer_en: Drift means the world moved and the model did not. Data drift is when the inputs change. Concept drift is when the same inputs now mean a different outcome. The model can stay confident while getting worse, so we have to watch it.
entries.followup_en: A new school mix is data drift. A grading policy change is concept drift. I would track input stats, prediction rates, and real outcomes when they arrive. A fixed golden set also tells me if a code change, not the world, broke quality.
entries.answer_ar: الانحراف يعني أن البيانات أو علاقة المدخلات بالنتيجة تغيّرت مع الوقت، فيبقى النموذج واثقاً بينما يسوء أداؤه.

entries.question: How do you monitor a model in production and know when to retrain?
aliases: how do you monitor a model in production
how do you know when to retrain
when do you retrain the model
what alerts do you put on a model
entries.answer_en: I watch inputs, prediction mix, and real outcomes when they arrive later. I keep a golden set and re-run it after every change. We agree a quality floor with the business. Crossing that floor is the retrain trigger, not a calendar alone.
entries.followup_en: I would not retrain automatically on unreviewed labels, especially in a ministry. Bad labels teach the next model the wrong lesson. Retrain is a release: same checks as the first launch, plus a diff against the last golden run. If only one department drifted, I investigate that slice first.
entries.answer_ar: أراقب توزيع المدخلات والتنبؤات والنتائج الحقيقية، وأعيد التدريب عندما يهبط الأداء دون الحد المتفق عليه بعد مراجعة بشرية للتسميات.

entries.question: What is a large language model?
aliases: what is a large language model
how is an llm different from a classifier
entries.answer_en: An LLM (Large Language Model) is an AI model trained on large amounts of text data to understand and generate human language.
entries.followup_en: That is why I wrap it. For BTEC questions I retrieve unit text first, force JSON with Pydantic, and a teacher approves before save. A classifier outputs a label from a fixed list. An LLM can draft, extract, or chat, but it needs those checks when the answer matters.

does an llm need a gpu

entries.question: What are the steps to create an LLM?
aliases: what are the steps to create an llm
what are the steps to train an llm
how do you train an llm
how would you train a large language model from scratch
walk me through the steps to create an llm
did you train a foundation model
entries.answer_en: Creating a foundation LLM is not the same as using one. You collect huge text, tokenize it, pre-train a Transformer, then align it with instructions. After that you evaluate and serve it. I have not trained a foundation model from scratch.
entries.followup_en: Pre-training is next-token prediction on many GPUs. Alignment is extra: supervised instruction data, then preference methods like RLHF or DPO. Serving adds quantization and an API. In my work I take a pretrained model and build the product around it: retrieval, prompts, structured output, and human approval.
entries.answer_ar: بناء نموذج أساس يمر بجمع النص والتقطيع والتدريب المسبق ثم المحاذاة والتقييم والنشر، وهذا عمل مختبرات؛ عملي يستخدم نموذجاً جاهزاً.

entries.question: How does an LLM work?
aliases: explain how a language model generates text
can you explain the main steps of how an llm processes text
how does the model generate text
how does an llm generate text
what happens inside an llm when it answers
walk me through next token prediction
entries.answer_en: An LLM works in steps: tokenization splits text into tokens, embeddings turn tokens into vectors, the transformer uses attention to understand context, then it predicts the next token and repeats until it generates a full response.
entries.followup_en: Tokenization → Embeddings → Transformer attention → Next-token prediction → Text generation.
entries.answer_ar: يعمل النموذج اللغوي بخطوات: التقطيع إلى رموز، التحويل إلى متجهات، الانتباه لفهم السياق، ثم التنبؤ بالرمز التالي مراراً حتى يكتمل الرد.

entries.question: What is a Transformer?
entries.answer_en: A Transformer is the neural design behind today's LLMs. Self-attention lets each token weigh how much every other token in the context matters. Tokens become embeddings, then stacked attention layers, then chances for the next token.
entries.followup_en: Attention is why the model can use nearby words to tell two meanings of the same token apart. It still only predicts the next token. I do not recite the equations in an interview. I need that picture, plus the practical limit: everything must fit in the context window.
entries.answer_ar: المحوّل هو معمارية النماذج اللغوية اليوم، وفكرته الانتباه الذاتي: كل رمز يزن أهمية الرموز الأخرى في السياق قبل التنبؤ بالتالي.

entries.question: What are the main uses of LLMs?
aliases: what can llms be used for
what are the main uses of llms
would you use an llm for this report
can an llm extract fields from a document
entries.answer_en: They are strong at answering over text, summarizing, translating, drafting, writing code, and pulling structured fields from messy language. In my work I use them for BTEC exam questions and feedback, grounded in course material. A human still checks what matters.
entries.followup_en: I do not use an LLM for the assignment similarity checker. That is embeddings and cosine similarity. I also do not use one for helpdesk routing or early-warning scores. Those were classic ML. An LLM earns its place when the task is open language, not a fixed label.
entries.answer_ar: النماذج اللغوية تفيد في الإجابة والتلخيص والصياغة واستخراج الحقول، واستخدمتها لتوليد أسئلة BTEC من محتوى الوحدة مع مراجعة المعلّم.

entries.question: What are the main problems and limitations of LLMs?
aliases: what are the main problems of llms
what are the limitations of large language models
what are the risks of using llms
what are the weaknesses of llms
what can go wrong with llms
why should we not trust the model alone
entries.answer_en: They invent fluent answers. They do not know your private files or last week's change. They cost money and time, especially with long prompts. External APIs raise privacy issues. Untrusted documents can inject instructions. Those are engineering problems, not just model bugs.
entries.followup_en: I handle them in four ways. Retrieval, so the answer has a source. Pydantic, so the shape is right. Permission for the model to say 'I do not know'. And hosting based on where the data may go. For BTEC, teacher approval comes after generation. None of this makes the model truthful on its own. It makes the system fail closed.
entries.answer_ar: أبرز حدودها الاختلاق، وغياب معرفة وثائقنا، والتكلفة والتأخير، وخصوصية البيانات، وحقن التعليمات عبر الملفات.

entries.question: What are tokens?
aliases: what is a token in an llm
why does arabic cost more tokens
entries.answer_en: A token is the unit the model reads: not a letter, not always a whole word. Tokenization splits text into those pieces. Arabic usually needs more tokens than English for the same meaning, so cost and context fill up faster.
entries.followup_en: That matters for RAG chunk sizes too. If I count words instead of tokens, Arabic chunks overflow. Billing, rate limits, and the context window are all in tokens. I would pick an embedding model that was actually tested on Arabic, not only on English benchmarks.
entries.answer_ar: الرمز هو وحدة قراءة النموذج بعد تقطيع النص، والعربية غالباً تستهلك رموزاً أكثر من الإنجليزية لنفس المعنى.

entries.question: What is the context window?
aliases: context window size affect the model
how does context window size affect performance
what is a context window in an llm and how does its size affect
what is a context window in an llm
what happens when the context is full
can I paste the whole pdf
does a bigger window replace rag
entries.answer_en: A context window is the maximum number of tokens an LLM can process in one context. A larger window allows more information, but it may increase memory usage and processing time.
entries.followup_en: A huge window helps, but it is slower and more expensive, and the model still gets lost in noise. Good retrieval beats stuffing. If history is long, I summarize or drop old turns. Overflow is not a soft error. The start of the prompt can be cut off.
entries.answer_ar: نافذة السياق هي الحد الأقصى لعدد الرموز التي يعالجها النموذج في سياق واحد. النافذة الأكبر تسمح بمزيد من المعلومات، لكنها قد تزيد الذاكرة ووقت المعالجة.

entries.question: What does temperature do?
aliases: what does temperature do in an llm
how do you make the model output deterministic
why is the answer different every time
entries.answer_en: Temperature controls the randomness of token selection. Lower values usually give more consistent answers, while higher values allow more variation.
entries.followup_en: Even at temperature zero, some stacks are not fully repeatable, and a fluent lie can still be the most likely continuation. I would not fight hallucination by turning a knob. I retrieve sources, require citations, and block numbers that are not in the text.
entries.answer_ar: درجة الحرارة تضبط عشوائية اختيار الرموز. القيم المنخفضة تعطي إجابات أكثر ثباتاً، والعالية تسمح بتنوّع أكبر.

entries.question: What is hallucination and why does it happen?
aliases: why does the model make things up
the answer sounded right but was false
entries.answer_en: Hallucination is when an LLM generates incorrect or unsupported information. We can reduce it using RAG, reliable data, clear prompts, and validation.
entries.followup_en: So I do not try to 'fix the brain'. I change the system: retrieve text, allow I do not know, check numbers against the source, and keep a human on actions. Low temperature only makes the lie more stable. It does not make it true.
entries.answer_ar: الاختلاق هو توليد معلومات غير صحيحة أو غير مدعومة. نقلّله بالاسترجاع وبيانات موثوقة وprompts واضحة والتحقق.

entries.question: How do you prevent or reduce hallucination?
aliases: how do you handle hallucination in your systems
how do you stop the model from hallucinating
how do you deal with hallucination
how do you force the model to stick to sources
entries.answer_en: We can reduce hallucination using RAG, reliable data, clear prompts, and validation.
entries.followup_en: On BTEC question generation, the unit content is retrieved first. The schema is checked with Pydantic. And a teacher saves it only after review. If retrieval returns nothing useful, I abstain. Prompt wording helps. But it is the check after the answer that really blocks invented numbers.
entries.answer_ar: نقلّل الاختلاق باستخدام الاسترجاع وبيانات موثوقة وprompts واضحة والتحقق من الإجابات.

entries.question: How do you write a good prompt?
aliases: how do you write a good prompt
how do you keep documents from becoming instructions
listen_for: do not treat document as command
entries.answer_en: A good prompt states the task, the inputs, the limits, and the output shape. I keep trusted instructions apart from document text, so a file cannot become a command. I test prompt changes on a fixed example set, not by feeling.
entries.followup_en: For classification I list allowed labels and what to do when it is unclear: return needs-review, never take an action. Few-shot examples help when the format is hard to describe. I store the prompt in code so diffs are reviewable. A clever sentence is not a substitute for schema checks.
entries.answer_ar: التعليمات الجيدة تحدّد المهمة والمدخلات والحدود وشكل الخرج، وتفصل الأوامر عن نص الوثائق، وتُختبر على مجموعة ثابتة.

entries.question: What is the difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting?
aliases: what is the difference between zero shot and few shot
when do you use few shot examples
does few shot change the model weights
why not put twenty examples in the prompt
entries.answer_en: Zero-shot is the task with no solved examples. Few-shot adds a few input-output samples in the prompt. Those samples are not training. The weights do not change. I use few-shot when the format or the label edges are hard to explain in words.
entries.followup_en: Each example burns tokens on every call, so I keep them short. If I need hundreds of examples, that is closer to fine-tuning or a classifier. For tickets, two or three good samples beat a long essay about policy. I still validate the output schema after.
entries.answer_ar: بدون أمثلة أصف المهمة فقط، ومع أمثلة قليلة أوضّح الشكل في الطلب نفسه دون تغيير أوزان النموذج.

entries.question: Why do you ask the model for JSON instead of free text?
aliases: why do you ask the model for json
why structured output instead of free text
how do you get reliable output from an llm
how do you use pydantic with an llm
what if the json is valid but the fact is wrong
entries.answer_en: JSON lets me check each field in code. A required source field means a citation-less answer is invalid. The next system can store it without parsing prose. I define the shape with Pydantic and drop anything that does not match.
entries.followup_en: A valid object can still be a lie. So a faithfulness check comes after it. In BTEC generation I reject extra keys, wrong types, and empty sources. If the model cannot fill the schema, I retry once. Then it goes to a teacher as failed, not as a guessed essay.
entries.answer_ar: أطلب JSON حتى أتحقق من الحقول بالمخطط، وأرفض الجواب بلا مصدر، مع العلم أن الشكل الصحيح لا يعني المعنى الصحيح.

entries.question: How do you decide between an external API like GPT and hosting a model yourself?
aliases: how do you decide between an external api and hosting a model yourself
openai api or open source model, which one
would you use gpt or a self hosted model
how do you choose an llm for a government organization
can this data leave the country
entries.answer_en: I start with the data, not the model brand. Public questions can use an external API. Budget or personal records should stay in-country, on a sovereign cloud or on-prem. I keep an abstraction so we can move later without rewriting the app.
entries.followup_en: Hardware and serving come after that legal line. A smaller open model plus good retrieval often beats a giant API for internal documents. I have not run vLLM in production. I would use it when we host ourselves and need many users on one GPU. Identity and logging stay in our network either way.
entries.answer_ar: قرار الاستضافة يبدأ بتصنيف البيانات: ما هو عام قد يخرج لواجهة سحابية، وما هو سيادي يبقى داخل الدولة مع طبقة تجريد لتبديل النموذج.

entries.question: What are the risks of sending financial data to an external API, and how do you mitigate them?
aliases: what are the risks of sending financial data to an external api
what are the risks of using openai with sensitive data
how do you protect data when using a cloud llm
what about data privacy with external models
does the vendor train on our prompts
how do you anonymize before calling gpt
entries.answer_en: The data may leave the country. The vendor may keep prompts. They can change the model or throttle us. The bill can grow without anyone noticing. If I must use an API, I strip identifiers, send the smallest context, and hide the vendor behind our own interface.
entries.followup_en: I would also want a written no-training, no-retention term, and a log of what left. Full ledger rows should not go in a prompt. For finance I would rather self-host or use a UAE sovereign option. The interface is what lets us switch without a rewrite.
entries.answer_ar: مخاطر الواجهة الخارجية الإقامة والاحتفاظ بالبيانات والاعتماد على المورّد والتكلفة؛ إن لزم استخدامها أُخفي الهويات وأرسل الحد الأدنى خلف طبقة تجريد.

entries.question: Have you built an on-premise LLM deployment before?
aliases: have you built an on premise llm deployment
have you deployed an llm on premise
have you self hosted a language model
have you deployed open source models in production
have you run llama on your own servers
what on prem experience do you actually have
entries.answer_en: Not with an LLM in production, no. I did run on-premise systems for years: government payments in Kuwait, no public internet. I know isolation, access control, uptime, and audit. The new piece for me is GPU sizing and serving.
entries.followup_en: I have studied VRAM math, quantization, and engines like vLLM, but I have not used vLLM in production. On the first GPU build I would want a senior infrastructure partner, then own operations after. I would rather say that now than hide it.
entries.answer_ar: لم أنشر نموذجاً لغوياً على الخوادم في الإنتاج، لكن لدي سنوات تشغيل أنظمة معزولة للمدفوعات، والجزء الجديد هو تخطيط المعالج الرسومي.

entries.question: How many GPUs do we need, and how do you size the hardware?
aliases: how many gpus do we need
how do you size gpu hardware for an llm
how much vram does a model need
what hardware do we need to run a model locally
can a 7b model fit on one card
do we need a 70 billion model
entries.answer_en: Weights come first: a 7B model in FP16 is about 14 GB, plus extra for the KV cache. Quantization to 8 or 4 bit cuts that a lot. Then I ask if we even need a model that big. Many document jobs work with a smaller model plus retrieval.
entries.followup_en: I size from the use case and how many users at once, not from a brochure. I have not used vLLM in production. I would use it so the card groups requests instead of sitting idle. Buying eight GPUs for a chatbot that ten people use is the wrong answer.
entries.answer_ar: أحسب الذاكرة من حجم الأوزان زائداً كاش الانتباه، ثم أسأل إن كان نموذج أصغر مع استرجاع يكفي قبل شراء البطاقات.

entries.question: What is the difference between Ollama and vLLM?
aliases: what is the difference between ollama and vllm
which model server would you use in production
entries.answer_en: Ollama is a local runner. I would use it to try a model on a laptop. vLLM is a production server: it batches requests and manages GPU memory so more users share one card. I have not used vLLM in production. I would use it when we self-host for real traffic.
entries.followup_en: Both can look like an OpenAI API, so the app should call one internal URL. Continuous batching is why vLLM wins on throughput. Ollama is fine for demos. Putting Ollama behind a ministry load is the mistake I would avoid.
entries.answer_ar: أولاما للتجربة المحلية، وvLLM محرك خدمة يدفع دفعات الطلبات على البطاقة؛ لم أستخدمه في الإنتاج لكنني سأختاره للتحميل الحقيقي.

entries.question: Are you familiar with Core42 or the UAE sovereign cloud options?
aliases: what do you know about g42
what sovereign cloud options exist in the uae
have you worked with uae ai providers
should we use a uae hosted model
entries.answer_en: I have not used Core42 in a project. I know it as part of G42: UAE cloud and AI that keeps data in the country. For a UAE government body, I would evaluate a sovereign option before any foreign API. The first question is where the data goes.
entries.followup_en: Smartest model is the wrong starting point if prompts cannot leave. I would still put an interface in front so we can switch providers. I would test Arabic quality on our own documents, not only on a vendor slide.
entries.answer_ar: لم أعمل مع Core42 مباشرة، وأعرفه خياراً سيادياً إماراتياً؛ لأي جهة حكومية أقيّم بقاء البيانات داخل الدولة قبل أي واجهة خارجية.

entries.question: Have you used SageMaker or Azure ML?
aliases: what is your experience with managed ml platforms
entries.answer_en: I have not used SageMaker or Azure ML in production. They are managed layers for training, endpoints, and monitoring. My equivalent is shipping models behind FastAPI and running the operations myself. If the ministry already lives on one cloud, I would follow that standard.
entries.followup_en: The identity, private network, and logging usually decide this, not a feature checklist. A platform saves ops and adds lock-in. I would wrap it behind the same generate interface I use for a local model, so we are not stuck.
entries.answer_ar: لم أستخدم SageMaker أو Azure ML في الإنتاج؛ نشرت النماذج خلف فاست إيه بي آي، وسألتزم بمنصة الوزارة إن كانت معياراً مع طبقة تجريد.

entries.question: What is RAG?
aliases: can you explain rag in simple terms
what is the idea behind rag
how do you answer from our documents
entries.answer_en: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a technique that retrieves relevant information from external sources and gives it to an LLM before generating an answer.
entries.followup_en: It exists because the model does not know internal files, and because we can show a source. When a unit changes, I re-index that file. I do not retrain the LLM. The assignment similarity checker is not RAG. That one only compares embeddings. No generation step.
entries.answer_ar: RAG تقنية تسترجع معلومات ذات صلة من مصادر خارجية وتعطيها للنموذج قبل توليد الجواب.

entries.question: Why do we use RAG?
entries.answer_en: We use RAG to give the LLM up-to-date and relevant information and reduce hallucination.
entries.followup_en: We use RAG to give the LLM up-to-date and relevant information and reduce hallucination.
entries.answer_ar: نستخدم RAG لإعطاء النموذج معلومات حديثة وذات صلة وتقليل الاختلاق.

entries.question: How would you build a RAG system?
aliases: how does a rag system work
how would you build a rag system
walk me through a rag architecture
how would you implement rag here
what are the steps of rag
walk me through how rag works
how would you build rag for our documents
entries.answer_en: In this project, I built a RAG system for PDF documents. First, the system reads the PDF and extracts the text using PyPDF2. Then I split the text into small chunks and convert them into embeddings using an embedding model such as OpenAI or Hugging Face. I store the embeddings in FAISS for similarity search. When the user asks a question, the system retrieves the most relevant chunks. Then LangChain sends the question and the relevant context to the LLM to generate the final answer.
entries.followup_en: PDF → extract → chunk → embed → FAISS → retrieve → LLM answer.
entries.answer_ar: بنيت نظام RAG لمستندات PDF: استخراج النص بـ PyPDF2، تقسيمه إلى أجزاء، تحويلها لتضمينات، تخزينها في FAISS، ثم استرجاع الأجزاء الأقرب وإرسال السؤال والسياق عبر LangChain إلى النموذج للجواب النهائي.

entries.question: What are the indexing and retrieval phases in RAG?

when do you embed the documents
entries.answer_en: Indexing organizes embeddings so the system can search and retrieve relevant information quickly. Retrieval is the live step that finds the best chunks for a question.
entries.followup_en: If indexing is wrong, no prompt fix will help. If indexing is right and the answer is still wrong, I inspect the prompt and the model. Components are chunker, embedding model, vector store, retriever, optional reranker, LLM, and validation. I have not used a cross-encoder reranker in production.

entries.question: What chunk size and overlap do you use?
aliases: what chunk size do you use
what chunk size and overlap do you use
how big should a chunk be
should I split by tokens or by heading
listen_for: three hundred to eight hundred tokens
entries.answer_en: There is no one number. For regulations I split on the natural unit: article, clause, section. As a start I use about 300 to 800 tokens with some overlap so a sentence is not cut. Then I test which setting actually retrieves the right clause.
entries.followup_en: Tiny chunks lose context. Huge chunks dump noise into the prompt and waste the window. Arabic uses more tokens, so I count tokens, not words. I would rather two settings A/B on real questions than a blog default. Headers in metadata help even when the split is imperfect.
entries.answer_ar: حجم المقطع يعتمد على نوع الوثيقة؛ أبدأ من حدود المواد القانونية ثم أجرّب بضع إعدادات على أسئلة حقيقية مع حساب الرموز لا الكلمات.

entries.question: Our regulations change every year. Should we fine-tune the model or use RAG?
aliases: should we fine tune the model or use rag
what is the difference between rag and fine tuning
when do you fine tune versus use retrieval
our documents change often, fine tuning or rag
entries.answer_en: RAG for the facts. Fine-tuning for behavior. When a regulation changes, I re-index that file and the system is current the same day. Fine-tuning cannot show the clause. I would fine-tune for tone, report shape, or terminology, not for yearly rules.
entries.followup_en: A citation is a product requirement in finance, not a nice extra. Retraining every year is slow and expensive, and the old weights still mix with the new. I have done only basic fine-tuning. For ministry knowledge I would still pick RAG first.
entries.answer_ar: المعرفة المتغيّرة مكانها الاسترجاع وإعادة الفهرسة، أما الضبط الدقيق فلسلوك النموذج ونبرته لا للمواد التي تتبدّل كل عام.

entries.question: A user from one department asks about a confidential document from another. What happens?
aliases: a user from one department asks about a confidential document from another department
how do you handle access control in rag
how do you make sure users only see documents they are allowed to
how do you handle permissions in retrieval
can the model leak another department file
do you filter before or after vector search
entries.answer_en: Nothing from that file is retrieved. I filter by the user's allowed set before similarity search, not after. Each chunk carries department and classification. If I searched first, the secret text would already sit in memory and in logs even if the user never saw it.
entries.followup_en: The LLM never gets a chance to summarize what it should not see. Identity comes from the app, not from the prompt. I would also strip denied docs from caches. Access control belongs in retrieval, not as a polite instruction to the model.
entries.answer_ar: لا يُسترجع الملف السرّي أصلاً: أصفي حسب صلاحية المستخدم قبل البحث، لأن التصفية بعده تسرّب النص إلى الذاكرة والسجلات.

entries.question: What is metadata filtering in RAG?
aliases: what is pre filtering in retrieval
what metadata do you store with chunks
entries.answer_en: Every chunk is stored with tags: department, year, type, classification. Metadata filtering means I search only inside the matching set, before I rank by meaning. It is for access control and for precision, like only 2024 rules.
entries.followup_en: If I retrieve twenty chunks then drop the secret ones, those secret ones were already scored and maybe logged. Pre-filter avoids that. It also stops an old policy from ranking above the new one just because the wording is similar. Bad metadata makes both security and quality fail.
entries.answer_ar: التصفية بالبيانات الوصفية تضيق البحث إلى المقاطع المسموحة والمطابقة للسنة أو النوع قبل حساب التشابه.

entries.question: How do you stop the system from inventing a number that is not in the documents?
aliases: how do you stop the system from inventing a number
how do you prevent hallucination in rag
how do you make sure the answer comes from the documents
how do you ground the model in the source
the model rounded the budget figure
entries.answer_en: I tell the model to use only the given text and to say I do not know. I require a source field in JSON. Then a check: every number in the answer must appear in the retrieved text, or I block it. A person still approves financial actions.
entries.followup_en: The instruction alone is weak. The hard gate is string or normalized match on amounts, dates, and IDs. If retrieval missed the clause, the system should abstain, not guess. I used the same idea on BTEC: generate from unit text, validate schema, teacher confirms.
entries.answer_ar: أمنع الأرقام المخترعة بالإجابة من النص فقط، وحقل مصدر إلزامي، ورفض أي رقم لا يظهر في المقاطع، مع موافقة بشرية للمالي.

entries.question: Could the system detect a conflict of interest between a supplier and an employee?
aliases: could the system detect a conflict of interest
how do you answer questions that span multiple documents
ownership in one file employment in another
why is vector search not enough here
would you use a knowledge graph for this
entries.answer_en: Not with vector search alone. Similarity finds text that looks like the question. A conflict is a path across files: ownership in one, job in another, tender in a third. That needs entities and relations. I have not used a knowledge graph in production. I would use one here.
entries.followup_en: I would model company, person, department, and award as nodes, then walk edges. Vector search still helps to pull the supporting letters. People call that GraphRAG. Shipping it without clean entity extraction just creates a messy graph. I would start with a few high-value relation types, not a full world model.
entries.answer_ar: البحث المتجهي لا يكفي لتعارض المصالح لأنه علاقة عبر وثائق متعددة؛ هنا أحتاج رسم معرفة، ولم أبنه في الإنتاج.

entries.question: What is a knowledge graph, and when would you use it instead of vector search?
aliases: when would you use a knowledge graph instead of vector search
when is the answer a path not a paragraph
entries.answer_en: A knowledge graph stores things as nodes and links as edges: this company is owned by this person. Vector search finds similar wording. I use vectors when the answer sits in one passage. I use a graph when the answer is a chain across facts. I have not built one in production.
entries.followup_en: GraphRAG is the mix: graph for the path, vectors for the documents you show. Graphs fail when names are messy or relations are wrong. They cost more to keep clean than a vector index. I would use them for conflicts, org charts, and supplier links, not for 'summarize this policy'.
entries.answer_ar: رسم المعرفة عقد وربط للعلاقات، بينما البحث المتجهي للمعنى في النص؛ أستخدم الرسم عندما يكون الجواب مساراً عبر عدة حقائق.

entries.question: Which vector database would you choose for us?
aliases: difference between pinecone qdrant chroma faiss
pinecone vs qdrant vs chroma vs faiss
what is the difference between pinecone qdrant chroma and faiss
which vector database would you choose
what vector database do you recommend
what is the difference between chroma and qdrant
listen_for: qdrant not in production for me
entries.answer_en: Pinecone and Qdrant are full vector databases, Chroma is simple and useful for local RAG, while FAISS is mainly a vector search library.
entries.followup_en: One less database means one less thing to back up and lock down. I would avoid a fully managed foreign cloud store for sovereign files. The choice is operations and filtering, not a beauty contest. Changing stores is easier if chunks and metadata already live in files we own.
entries.answer_ar: Pinecone وQdrant قواعد بيانات متجهات كاملة، وChroma بسيطة ومفيدة لـ RAG محلي، بينما FAISS أساساً مكتبة بحث متجهي.

entries.question: What is ChromaDB?
aliases: did you use chroma in production
entries.answer_en: Chroma is an open-source embedding store. A collection holds an id, a vector, the original text, and metadata. At query time I take nearest neighbors, optionally with a where filter. I used it in-process for prototypes. I have not run it as ministry production storage.
entries.followup_en: Smaller distance means closer, and cosine versus L2 changes the number. If I change the embedding model I rebuild the collection. It is convenient because there is no extra server. For production I would still compare Qdrant or pgvector on backup, users, and filters. I have not used Qdrant in production either.
entries.answer_ar: كروما قاعدة تضمين مفتوحة تخزّن المتجه والنص والواصفات، واستخدمتها في النماذج الأولية داخل بايثون لا كمخزن إنتاج وزاري.

entries.answer_en: I give it one clear job and a small set of tools. Anything that changes money or records waits for a human. I log every tool call. I save state so we can pause and resume. The model chooses the tool. My code runs it, after the checks.
entries.followup_en: Read-only search can be autonomous. Posting a payment cannot. I would rather a refused action than a silent write. Narrow tools beat one 'run any SQL' tool. I have not used LangGraph in production, but I would want checkpoints and a human interrupt for that pause.

entries.question: What if the agent makes a mistake and performs a wrong action?

how do you make agents safe

entries.answer_en: It should not be able to complete a money action alone. A human approves first. I also cap steps and cost so it cannot loop. Tools are narrow: a report agent cannot write. Retries must be idempotent. The log of state is how we see what happened.
entries.followup_en: If a write did happen, the log plus idempotency keys tell us whether to reverse or skip. A generic retry is how you double-pay. I learned that in payment systems, not in LLM blogs. The same rule applies when an agent calls a tool twice after a timeout.
entries.answer_ar: الخطأ لا يُسمح له أن يصل لأثر مالي وحده: موافقة بشرية، حد للخطوات، أدوات ضيقة، وإعادة محاولة لا تكرر الأثر.

entries.question: How many tools do you give an agent, and how do you scope their permissions?
aliases: how many tools do you give an agent
how do you scope agent permissions
how do you secure the tools an agent can use
what is least privilege for agents
would you give the agent sql access
why too many tools confuse the model
entries.answer_en: As few as possible. Each extra tool is extra risk and extra confusion for the model. Least privilege sits on the tool: read-only, one table, one department. I never hand out run-any-SQL. A money tool should create an approval request, not execute.
entries.followup_en: I validate arguments in code, not in the prompt. Every call is logged, with its input and output. That log is the audit. If two jobs need different rights, I split agents rather than widen one toolbox. Wide tools are how prompt injection becomes a write.
entries.answer_ar: أقل عدد ممكن من الأدوات، كل واحدة بأقل صلاحية، واستعلامات ثابتة بدل SQL حر، وأي أثر مالي يتحول لطلب موافقة.

entries.question: What is tool calling?
aliases: how does an llm call a tool
does the model execute the function
how do you bind tools to a model
entries.answer_en: Function calling allows an LLM to request an external tool or API to perform a task. The application executes the call and returns the result.
entries.followup_en: Arguments go through a schema. If the model asks for a table it should not see, the tool refuses. Parallel tool calls need the same checks. This is how an agent is actually built. Without it you only have a chatbot that pretends to act.
entries.answer_ar: استدعاء الدوال يتيح للنموذج طلب أداة أو واجهة خارجية. التطبيق ينفّذ الطلب ويعيد النتيجة.

entries.question: When do you need multiple agents instead of one?
aliases: when do you need multiple agents
what is a multi agent system
what is an orchestrator or supervisor agent
entries.answer_en: I start with one agent. I split it in three cases. When tools need different rights. When a cheap model can do the routing. Or when the prompt is so long that the agent loses focus. Then a supervisor sends the work to specialists, and each one keeps a small set of tools.
entries.followup_en: In a ministry, permissions are usually the real reason: procurement data and finance data should not share one agent memory. Multi-agent also means more failure points and more tokens. I would not split for a demo diagram. I split when isolation or focus is a measured problem.
entries.answer_ar: أبدأ بوكيل واحد، وأفصل عندما تختلف الصلاحيات أو يطول السياق؛ عندها مشرف يوجّه لمتخصصين بأدوات ضيقة.

entries.question: What is ReAct and how do agents reason?
aliases: what reasoning patterns do agents use
entries.answer_en: ReAct is reason, act, observe, repeat. The model writes a thought, calls a tool, reads the result, then thinks again. Plan-and-execute writes the full plan first. That text is not real thinking. It is useful because I can read the steps. I never treat them as proof.
entries.followup_en: A nice chain can still justify a wrong tool. I cap the loop and I validate tool arguments. For audit, plan-and-execute is clearer than a messy ReAct trace. I still check the final action against policy, not against how pretty the thoughts looked.
entries.answer_ar: ReAct حلقة فكر ثم أداة ثم ملاحظة؛ هذا النص ليس تفكيراً حقيقياً لكنه مفيد للمراجعة، ولا أعتبره برهاناً على الصحة.

entries.question: What is chain of thought?
aliases: what is chain of thought prompting
should we show the hidden reasoning
why ask the model to think step by step
entries.answer_en: Chain of thought means the model writes steps in text before the final answer. It often helps on multi-step tasks, and I can read those steps. It is still generated language, not a proof. I use it for transparency. I do not trust it as truth.
entries.followup_en: In a user-facing app I may keep the chain internal so it does not leak private reasoning or tool names. For math-like tasks it helps. For citations it does not replace a source check. If the steps look right and the number is not in the document, the number still fails.
entries.answer_ar: سلسلة الفكر أن يكتب النموذج خطوات قبل الجواب؛ تفيد في المهام المتعددة لكنها ليست برهاناً، وأتحقق من النتيجة بالمصدر.

entries.answer_en: I use LangChain and LangGraph. LangChain helps connect LLMs with tools, and LangGraph helps manage agent workflows, state, and decision-making. I can also use Dify, n8n, and CrewAI when the case fits: Dify and n8n for visual workflows, and CrewAI for multi-agent setups.

entries.question: What is the difference between a library, a framework, and a platform?
aliases: what is the difference between a library a framework and a platform
what is a platform in ai
entries.answer_en: A library you call, like Pandas. A framework calls your code and sets the structure, like LangChain. A platform is where deploy, monitor, and permissions live, like SageMaker. Leaving a library is cheap. Leaving a platform is expensive.
entries.followup_en: I have not used SageMaker in production. I still want that distinction when a vendor says it is just a library. If identity, logs, and GPUs all sit there, it is a platform decision. I wrap it so the rest of the app still speaks generate and retrieve.
entries.answer_ar: المكتبة تستدعيها أنت، والإطار يستدعي شفرتك، والمنصة تسكن داخلها التشغيل والصلاحيات؛ كلفة الخروج ترتفع بهذا الترتيب.

entries.question: How do you avoid vendor lock-in?
aliases: how do you avoid vendor lock in
how do you avoid depending on one provider
how do you make the system model agnostic
how do you switch embedding providers
entries.answer_en: The app asks for generate or retrieve. It does not ask for OpenAI by name. Documents, chunks, and metadata stay in storage we own, so we can re-index elsewhere. I prefer tools that can run offline. A cloud-only box is lock-in by design.
entries.followup_en: OpenAI-compatible servers help, but the prompt and schema still need to be ours. Embeddings lock you until you reindex, so I version that model id. In BTEC I could change the chat model without rewriting the teacher flow. That was the point of the interface.
entries.answer_ar: أتجنب الارتباط بمورّد بواجهة داخلية للتوليد والاسترجاع، وبتخزين الوثائق عندنا حتى نعيد الفهرسة بأداة أخرى.

entries.question: Is n8n a good option for non-technical teams to automate processes?
aliases: what do you think about low code automation tools
n8n or zapier or power automate
can business users build the workflow
entries.answer_en: For connecting systems, yes, especially because n8n can be self-hosted. A manager can see the boxes. It is weaker at tests and version control. I would keep policy and money math in tested code, and let n8n call that code. I have not used n8n in production.
entries.followup_en: Zapier is easier and usually leaves the building. Power Automate fits a Microsoft shop but is not my default for sovereign data. Visual workflows drift when everyone edits them. One reviewed API for the rule, n8n for routing, is the split I would defend.
entries.answer_ar: n8n مناسب للربط البصري ويمكن استضافته داخلياً، لكن قواعد المال والسياسة تبقى في شفرة مختبرة؛ لم أشغّله في الإنتاج.

entries.question: What is n8n?
aliases: how is n8n different from langchain
entries.answer_en: n8n is workflow automation: visual nodes that connect apps, APIs, and data. It can be self-hosted. It can also host AI agent nodes, but I treat it as an integrator, not as the place where policy lives. I have not run it in production. I would use it for routing.
entries.followup_en: LangChain is code around models. n8n is ops around systems. An auditor can screenshot an n8n flow. They cannot unit-test it as easily as Python. So n8n starts FastAPI. Then FastAPI does the checks, the LLM call, and the audit log.
entries.answer_ar: n8n منصة أتمتة بصرية قابلة للاستضافة الداخلية لربط الأنظمة؛ ليست مكان منطق السياسة، ولم أستخدمها في الإنتاج.

entries.followup_en: The ideas transfer: prompts, tools, retrieval, identity. If the ministry standard is Google or Azure, I follow it and wrap the model. I would not fight a platform war on day one. I would still keep our documents and schemas outside the vendor SDK.

entries.question: How does speech-to-text work?
aliases: how does speech to text work
how does whisper turn audio into text
what happens after we capture the microphone
entries.answer_en: We capture audio, clean it, and often use VAD to drop silence. The model turns sound into features and decodes text. Whisper takes audio, processes it, recognizes the spoken words, and converts them into text.
entries.followup_en: In the Al Najat kiosk I used Whisper for that decode. Quality depends on noise, mic, and dialect, so I measure word error rate on our own recordings. Garbage audio in means garbage text out, before any later AI even starts.
entries.answer_ar: نلتقط الصوت وننظّفه وغالباً نستخدم VAD لإسقاط الصمت. النموذج يحوّل الصوت إلى ميزات ثم إلى نص. Whisper يأخذ الصوت ويعالجه ويتعرّف على الكلام ويحوّله إلى نص.

entries.question: How would you build a voice assistant?
aliases: how would you build a voice assistant
how do you design a speech system
what is your approach to speech recognition systems
how would you build a voice interface
walk me through a kiosk voice flow
listen_for: kiosk was not an llm agent
entries.answer_en: Capture audio, cut silence, run Whisper locally, then send the text onward. In the kiosk at Al Najat that next step was search and a simple reply, not an LLM agent. I measure error rate on our speakers. I delete the audio after I keep the text.
entries.followup_en: Voice is not a login factor by itself. If we add spoken answers, TTS is a separate model. Low-confidence transcripts should ask the user to confirm. For a ministry I would keep the same local STT default so recordings never leave.
entries.answer_ar: المساعد الصوتي يلتقط الصوت، يحوّله محلياً بنموذج مثل ويسبير، ثم يمرّر النص؛ في الكشك لم يكن ذلك وكيلاً لغوياً.

entries.question: Why Whisper and not a cloud speech API?
